# Security Review: `portal/portal_payment.php` **Verdict: Do not merge.** The change adds a new unauthenticated path to decrypted cardholder data (`recid`) and exposes a gateway key to the browser. It also builds on, and keeps, several pre-existing critical flaws in how patient identity and payment posting are authorized. --- ## Critical ### 1. IDOR via new `recid` parameter discloses any patient's card data - **Location:** `$recid = isset($_REQUEST['recid']) ? (int) $_REQUEST['recid'] : 0;` → `$edata = $appsql->getPortalAuditRec($recid);` → `$ccdata = json_decode(decryptStandard($edata['checksum']), true);` - **Category:** A01 Broken Access Control - **Problem:** - Any portal-logged-in patient can supply an arbitrary `recid`. The code does not check that the audit record belongs to `$_SESSION['pid']`, and does not restrict this parameter to staff. - The record is decrypted and rendered: cardholder name, zip, card number, expiry, CVV, transaction ID and auth code. - Sequential integer IDs make enumeration trivial. - The new display branch `if (isset($_SESSION['authUserID']) || isset($ccdata["transId"]))` prints the **full unmasked card number** to *anyone*, including patients, whenever a `transId` exists. - **Fix:** - Accept `recid` only for authenticated staff. - For any record lookup, verify `$edata['patient_id'] == $_SESSION['pid']` when `$isPortal`. - Never print the full PAN based on `transId`. ### 2. Patient ID taken from request, overriding the portal session (pre-existing, relied upon) - **Location:** - `$pid = isset($_REQUEST['pid']) ? $_REQUEST['pid'] : $pid;` - `$pid = $_REQUEST['hidden_patient_code'] > 0 ? $_REQUEST['hidden_patient_code'] : $pid;` - `$form_pid = $_POST['form_pid'];` - **Category:** A01 Broken Access Control - **Problem:** - A portal user's `$_SESSION['pid']` is replaced by attacker-controlled input. - The page then shows the other patient's name, insurance, encounter reasons, balances and pending card data (via `getPortalAudit($pid, ...)`). - Write operations then run against `$form_pid`. - The new `$isPortal` flag exists but is never used to block this. - **Fix:** When `$isPortal` is true, force `$pid = $form_pid = $_SESSION['pid']` and ignore all request-supplied patient identifiers. ### 3. Portal patients can post payments and close encounters without paying (pre-existing, modified in this diff) - **Location:** The whole `if ($_POST['form_save'])` block. - **Category:** A01 Broken Access Control / A04 Insecure Design - **Problem:** - Nothing requires `$_SESSION['authUserID']` before writing to `ar_session`, `ar_activity` and `payments`. - With `radio_type_of_payment=cash`, the code also runs `UPDATE form_encounter SET last_level_closed=4` and `UPDATE billing SET billed=1`. - The UI hides the "Post Payment" button from patients, but a patient can POST `form_save` directly. That lets them: - record arbitrary "payments" that were never charged, - mark encounters as closed or billed, for themselves or for any `form_pid`. - Amounts are server-unvalidated. Negative values pass `if ($amount = 0 + $payment)`, and `form_prepayment` is inserted raw. The "no negative payments" rule is client-side JS only. - **Fix:** - Require an authenticated staff user with the appropriate ACL (e.g. `acct`) for `form_save`. - Validate that amounts are positive numerics on the server. - Tie posted payments to a verified gateway transaction. ### 4. Storage and display of full PAN and CVV (pre-existing, retained) - **Location:** - `echo $ccdata["cardNumber"]` - `` - The InHouse flow posting raw card fields to `paylib.php` - **Category:** A02 Cryptographic Failures / A04 Insecure Design - **Problem:** - In the InHouse path, card number, expiry and CVV are stored (reversibly encrypted with the application key) in the portal audit table and shown to staff. - Storing the CVV after authorization is prohibited by PCI DSS under any circumstances. - Any database plus key compromise, or any IDOR (#1, #2), exposes full card data. - The AuthorizeNet and Stripe tokenization paths are an improvement, but the InHouse path remains the default (`paySubmit`). - **Fix:** - Remove the InHouse raw-card flow, or at minimum never persist CVV. - Store only a token and the last 4 digits. - Never render the full PAN. --- ## High ### 5. Gateway API key exposed to every page viewer - **Location:** `var apiKey = ;` - **Category:** A02 Cryptographic Failures / A05 Security Misconfiguration - **Problem:** - The key is emitted unconditionally to every portal and staff session, whichever gateway is configured. - For Stripe, the client only needs the publishable key (`publicKey`). If `gateway_api_key` holds the Stripe **secret** key, or an Authorize.Net transaction key rather than the login ID, attackers get full gateway API access: charges, refunds, customer data. - **Fix:** - Emit only the values the client library actually requires: Stripe publishable key; Authorize.Net `apiLoginID` and public `clientKey`. - Emit them only for the active gateway. - Keep secret keys server-side. ### 6. Stored XSS through the card number field - **Location:** `echo $ccdata["cardNumber"] . "
";` - **Category:** A03 Injection (XSS) - **Problem:** - `cardNumber` is patient-supplied, and the HTML `pattern` attribute is not enforced server-side. - It is echoed without escaping. A patient can submit `` as a "card number", and it executes in a staff (billing) user's session when they review the payment. - That enables session riding and access to all patient records. - Other fields were switched to `text()` in this diff, but this one was missed. - **Fix:** `echo text($ccdata["cardNumber"])`, and validate digits-only on the server. ### 7. No CSRF protection on state-changing requests - **Location:** - `invoiceForm` POST to `portal_payment.php` (`form_save`) - All POSTs to `lib/paylib.php` (`portal-save`, `review-save`, AuthorizeNet, Stripe) - **Category:** A01 Broken Access Control (CSRF) - **Problem:** No CSRF token is generated or verified. A malicious page can make a logged-in staff member post payments, close encounters or mark billing as billed. - **Fix:** Add and verify CSRF tokens (OpenEMR's `CsrfUtils`) on all of these requests. --- ## Medium ### 8. No accountable user recorded for portal-originated writes - **Location:** - `user_id = $_SESSION['authUserID']` and `post_user = $_SESSION['authUserID']` in `ar_session`/`ar_activity` inserts - Copay path uses `$_SESSION['authId']` - `sqlQueryNoLog` - **Category:** A09 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures - **Problem:** - When a portal patient triggers these writes, the user fields are empty or NULL. Financial records then have no attributable actor. - The change also replaced a hard-coded `post_user` of `3` with session values that are empty for portal users. - The inconsistent use of `authId` vs `authUserID` makes the audit trail unreliable. - **Fix:** - Once #3 is fixed, consistently record the staff user. - Log portal-originated payment events explicitly, including the patient pid. ### 9. Request body built by unencoded string concatenation - **Location:** `let extra = "&inv_values=" + inv_values + "&extra_values=" + extra_values;` (used with `.serialize() + extra`) - **Category:** A03 Injection (parameter injection) / A08 Data Integrity - **Problem:** The JSON is not URL-encoded. Values containing `&` or `=` inject or override POST parameters such as `pid` or `mode` seen by `paylib.php`. This compounds #2. - **Fix:** Wrap the values in `encodeURIComponent(...)`, or send a `FormData` or JSON body. ### 10. Race condition in `sequence_no` allocation - **Location:** `SELECT IFNULL(MAX(sequence_no),0) + 1 ...` inside `sqlBeginTrans()`, followed by an insert. - **Category:** A04 Insecure Design (integrity) - **Problem:** - Under InnoDB's default isolation, a plain `SELECT MAX` takes no lock. Concurrent postings can compute the same sequence number, causing duplicate-key failures or lost or misattributed ledger rows. - Writes to `ar_session` and `payments` sit outside the transaction, so partial failures leave inconsistent financial records. - **Fix:** - Use `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` or an atomic counter. - Wrap the whole payment posting in one transaction. --- ## Low ### 11. Wrong escaping context in JavaScript strings - **Location:** - `prompt("", ...)` - Various `alert("")` - **Category:** A03 Injection (XSS) - **Problem:** HTML escaping and `addslashes` are not correct for a JS string context. Exploitable only through malicious translation strings. - **Fix:** Use `json_encode()` (or `xlj()`), as the diff already does for `chargeMsg`. ### 12. Unescaped configuration values in HTML and JS - **Location:** `$GLOBALS['assets_static_relative']`, `$GLOBALS['webroot']`, `$v_js_includes` echoed raw into `src`/`action` attributes and JS strings. - **Category:** A03 Injection / A05 Security Misconfiguration - **Problem:** These are admin-controlled values, so this is defense in depth only. - **Fix:** Wrap them with `attr()` or `js_escape()`. ### 13. Third-party payment scripts not shown or controlled - **Location:** `Accept.dispatchData(...)` and `Stripe(publicKey)` are called, but no script includes appear in this diff. - **Category:** A08 Software and Data Integrity Failures / A06 Vulnerable and Outdated Components - **Problem:** The gateway libraries' load location and integrity are not visible in this change. - **Fix:** - Confirm they load only from the official gateway origins (`js.stripe.com`, `js.authorize.net`) over HTTPS. - Do not self-host or proxy them (Stripe requires direct loading). - Add a CSP restricting script sources. --- ## Summary | # | Issue | OWASP | Severity | New / Pre-existing | |---|-------|-------|----------|--------------------| | 1 | `recid` IDOR; full PAN shown when `transId` set | A01 | Critical | New | | 2 | Request `pid` overrides portal session | A01 | Critical | Pre-existing, relied upon | | 3 | Patients can post payments and close encounters; no server-side amount validation | A01/A04 | Critical | Pre-existing, modified | | 4 | PAN and CVV stored and displayed | A02/A04 | Critical | Pre-existing, retained | | 5 | Gateway API key sent to browser | A02/A05 | High | New | | 6 | Unescaped `cardNumber` (stored XSS) | A03 | High | Pre-existing, touched | | 7 | No CSRF tokens | A01 | High | Pre-existing | | 8 | No accountable user on portal writes | A09 | Medium | Pre-existing, modified | | 9 | Unencoded parameter concatenation | A03/A08 | Medium | Pre-existing, touched | | 10 | `sequence_no` race; non-atomic posting | A04 | Medium | New | | 11 | Wrong escaping in JS strings | A03 | Low | Pre-existing | | 12 | Unescaped config values | A03/A05 | Low | Pre-existing | | 13 | Gateway script integrity unverified | A08/A06 | Low | New |
